title: Chronological Evidence Bundler for RTBF Audits and Cross-Region Retention Compliance
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Build a server-side Evidence Bundler that assembles time-ordered, cryptographically stamped artifacts for each automated deletion (RTBF/retention) so customers and auditors receive a single verifiable package per deletion request. The bundler must correlate deletion events across replicas and regions, include redaction-safe manifests, and produce a customer-facing export and an internal attestation record.

Goals:
- Produce a signed, chronological evidence package (ZIP + manifest) for every completed RTBF or retention-driven deletion that includes: expunge logs, storage object digests, KMS-derived signature checkpoint, region stamps, and policy metadata.
- Support cross-region correlation: if data has replicas in EU + US, the package must show per-region deletion timestamps and a derived global deletion timeline.
- Offer two export modes: "full-evidence" (complete logs for auditors) and "redacted-customer" (PII removed, high-level proof + redaction map).
- Integrate with Console: per-request evidence link and retention timeline visualization.
- Ensure evidence generation is efficient (target extra cost < 2% of delete operation costs) and does not violate SLOs for deletion flows.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing legal template language for attestations — Legal will provide wording to be embedded.
- Not a replacement for full forensic exports for incident response; those are separate flows.

Acceptance criteria:
- For a sample of 500 RTBF requests in staging, evidence bundles generated successfully with valid KMS signatures and manifest checksums; bundles surface in Console and downloadable via API.
- Evidence package schema documented in Confluence and validated by Security & Legal.
- Rollout docs and safe-fallback strategy exist (can disable bundler per-tenant).

Design notes / decisions made so far:
- Chosen approach: incremental checkpointing. Each deletion pipeline step emits a lightweight event (expunge-requested, object-removed, index-pruned, db-row-deleted). A Bundler service consumes these events and assembles the bundle once a terminal state (deleted+replicated) is reached.
- Cryptographic anchoring: use customer KMS wrapping key to sign bundle manifest if tenant-managed keys are configured; otherwise use Redwood signing key and include key metadata. Signatures are detached and verifiable with public key published to the tenant's audit ledger.
- Cross-region correlation: Bundler waits for region-confirmed receipts (with region timestamp and storage digest). To bound latency, we use a configurable window (default 48 hours) after deletion to include late confirmations; bundles created after the window will link to follow-up proof patches.
- Storage plan: bundles stored in an immutable, write-once bucket with lifecycle policy matching retention echo for evidence (30 days by default, configurable per-contract).

APIs & UX:
- Console: per-tenant "Deletion history" page shows timeline, status, and download button for evidence bundle.
- API: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/purges/{purge_id}/evidence?action=generate to force-generation; GET to fetch bundle metadata.
- Export format: ZIP with manifest.json (flattened entries), per-item digest list, signatures/, region-stamps.json, redaction-map.json (if redacted), and a human-readable summary.txt.

Operational considerations:
- Cost: compute and storage for evidence archiving estimated at ~1.5% of deletion pipeline cost in baseline. We will monitor via cost-center tag and add budget alerts.
- Reliability: Bundler must be idempotent; replays should not create duplicate bundles. Use dedupe by purge_id + checksum.
- Compliance: Legal & Security must approve manifest fields. Include opt-in for tenant-managed KMS keys (security asked for HSM-backed signing support).

Open decisions / trade-offs:
1) Window length for late replica confirmation (24h vs 48h vs 7d). Tradeoff between timeliness and completeness. We currently default to 48h and provide per-tenant override.
2) Whether to include raw storage logs in "full-evidence" vs a digest reference to logs retained in internal audit store. Due to privacy, prefer digests by default and raw logs only for legal-approved exports.
3) Retention of evidence bundles: default 30 days vs contract-driven 7 years. Implementation will support contract-configured retention with Admin control.

QA & rollout plan:
- Stage: generate bundles for synthetic RTBF runs; run verifier that checks KMS signatures and manifest integrity.
- Canary 1: 5% of new RTBFs for small tenants (non-contract) with Console link only.
- Canary 2: 100% for a single pilot enterprise customer with legal & security present.
- Full rollout: gated on pilot sign-offs, cost within thresholds, and Security review completion.

Telemetry & monitoring:
- Bundle generation success rate, time-to-bundle histogram, size distribution, KMS sign failures, and storage cost metrics.
- Alerts: >2% generation failure rate for 1h, KMS exception spike, or average time-to-bundle > configured window.

Integration & tasks for other teams:
- ENG (Serving/Platform): implement immutable bundle storage and provide expunge events. (See ENG-18872, ENG-19105).
- Security: review manifest schema and KMS signing flow.
- Legal: provide attestation text and rules for raw log disclosures.
- Console: UI for per-purge evidence access and timeline visualization.

Deliverables:
- Confluence spec and schema: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMPLIANCE/Chronological+Evidence+Bundler (draft)
